label: S-A2 wrong key: the 4 kg box gains twice the energy, key says the same

item.question_text: A 2 kg box and a 4 kg box are both lifted from the floor onto the same table. Compare the increase in the energy in their gravitational potential energy stores.

options.a: It is the same for both boxes
options.b: It is twice as much for the 4 kg box
options.c: It is half as much for the 4 kg box
options.d: It is four times as much for the 4 kg box

feedback.b: The boxes are lifted through the same height, so they gain the same energy.
feedback.c: The heavier box does not gain less energy: both rise the same height.
feedback.d: Energy does not depend on the square of the mass.

misconception_map.b: slip: thinks more mass means more energy stored
misconception_map.c: slip: inverted the relationship with mass

item.explanation: Both boxes rise through the same height, so the increase in their gravitational potential energy stores is the same.

label: S-B2 out of specification: variation of g with height (not GCSE)

item.question_text: A satellite is lifted to an orbit 400 km above the Earth's surface. Why would using g = 9.8 N/kg in the gravitational potential energy equation give the wrong value for the energy needed?

options.a: The gravitational field strength is smaller at that height
options.b: The satellite has no mass once it is in orbit
options.c: The equation only works for objects touching the ground
options.d: The height is too small compared with the Earth to matter

feedback.b: The satellite's mass does not change in orbit.
feedback.c: The equation applies to changes in height above the ground as well.
feedback.d: 400 km is large enough for g to change noticeably.

misconception_map.b: slip: thinks objects in orbit have no mass
misconception_map.c: slip: thinks the equation only applies at ground level

item.explanation: g decreases with distance from the Earth's centre. At 400 km it is about 8.7 N/kg, so using 9.8 N/kg for the whole height overestimates the energy.

label: S-C1 mastery check with a filler distractor (d) and a mismatched mapping (a)

item.question_text: A box is lifted onto a shelf. Which change would increase the energy transferred to its gravitational potential energy store?

options.b: Lifting it onto a higher shelf
options.c: Using a longer ramp to reach the same shelf
options.d: Painting the box a lighter colour

feedback.a: Lifting more slowly changes the power, not the energy stored.
feedback.c: Only the vertical height gained matters, not the length of the ramp.
feedback.d: The colour of the box has no effect on the energy stored.

misconception_map.d: slip: thinks colour affects the energy stored

item.explanation: Ep = mass × g × height gained, so only a greater mass, or a greater vertical height, increases it.
